docs.title: BioPAT® Spectro UV Server Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the BioPAT® Spectro UV Server documentation! This system provides real-time 201-wavelength UV-Vis spectroscopy acquisition and industrial OPC UA publication for Sartorius BioPAT® Spectro UV / tec5 spectrometers.

docs.title: What is BioPAT Spectro UV Server?
docs.text:
In industrial biomanufacturing and laboratory bioprocess monitoring, UV-Vis spectrometers capture continuous absorption curves across hundreds of wavelengths. However, standard automation setups usually constrain operators to extracting only 1 to 4 fixed wavelengths for DCS/SCADA historians.

BioPAT Spectro UV Server unlocks 201 simultaneous wavelengths (190 nm to 390 nm in 1 nm increments): - Direct UDP Ingestion: Captures high-frequency 840-byte UDP broadcasts from the tec5 tecSaaS MPT software (the vendor control application driving the spectrometer) — 5 datagrams per cycle, one per data type. - Microservices Architecture: Runs as a 4-container Docker stack (udpparser, redisserver, opcserver, udphelper). - Industrial Standards Compliance: Publishes full spectral arrays over OPC UA (opc.tcp://<host>:4841) to SCADA, DeltaV, Ignition, or OSIsoft PI. - Hardware-Free Testing: Includes a mock UDP emitter to simulate full UV-Vis spectra with zero hardware attached. - Automated Recovery: A Redis watchdog (udphelper) flags stale spectral data so the optional Windows tray companion can restart the spectrometer's measurement session automatically.

docs.title: Quick Command Reference
docs.text:
# Clone and start the stack
git clone https://github.com/Sir-Narwhal/biopat-spectrouv-server.git
cd biopat-spectrouv-server
docker compose up -d

# Run simulated spectra test
python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The BioPAT® Spectro UV Server is designed around a decoupled, microservices architecture using Docker Compose and Redis as a real-time in-memory message bus.

docs.title: 1. Ingestion (udpparser)
docs.text:
• Binds to 0.0.0.0:20202 (UDP).
  • Receives 840-byte datagrams from the tec5 tecSaaS MPT software — the vendor application that drives the spectrometer and does the actual UDP broadcasting (the spectrometer hardware itself has no network interface here). Every acquisition cycle sends up to 5 of these datagrams, one per data type (sample, onlinereference, transmission, absorbance, calibration).
  • Parses the 36-byte header: verifies length (840), extracts point count (201), wavelength bounds (190.0–390.0 nm), and data type code.
  • Unpacks 201 float32 values.
  • Writes JSON arrays into Redis with a 5-second TTL (ex=5) to prevent stale measurements if transmission ceases.
  • Channel assignment is manual, not auto-detected. The packet header does carry a channel index (bytes 18–19, see below), but udpparser never reads it — every value it writes is tagged with whatever UDP_CHANNEL_NAME is set to in compose.yaml/.env (channel_1 by default). Setting this correctly for your actual wiring is required; see Setup & Deployment.

docs.title: 2. State & Message Bus (redisserver)
docs.text:
• Operates in-memory on port 6379.
  • Decouples high-frequency network packets from OPC UA client polling.

docs.title: 3. Industrial Publication (opcserver)
docs.text:
• Hosts standard OPC UA server on port 4841 (opc.tcp://0.0.0.0:4841).
  • Namespace: http://biopat/spectrouv.
  • Updates writable variables for each channel every 1 second.

docs.title: 4. Session Watchdog (udphelper)
docs.text:
• Polls the absorbance_channel_1 key in Redis once per second.
  • If the key is missing (expired TTL, meaning no fresh UDP data), sets mpt_refresh = "true" in Redis and logs a warning.
  • Re-arms itself once fresh absorbance data reappears, so it can raise the flag again if data goes stale a second time. The mpt_refresh key itself is cleared by the tray application after it finishes handling the restart.
  • Has no direct network exposure — it only communicates via Redis. The mpt_refresh key is polled by the MPT Guardian tray companion, which reacts by restarting the tec5 measurement session. MPT Guardian, tecSaaS MPT, and this whole Docker Compose stack all run on the same Windows PC in the recommended deployment (via Docker Desktop) — Guardian talks to redisserver over localhost, not over the network.
  • MPT Guardian is optional for short test sessions, but mandatory for any session longer than ~6 hours — the tec5 tecSaaS MPT software intermittently stops transmitting UDP data on its own over long runs, and this watchdog/tray-app pair is the only thing that detects and recovers from it automatically. Without MPT Guardian installed, absorbance_channel_1 simply stays stale with no automatic recovery.

docs.title: UDP Packet Structure (840 Bytes)
docs.text:
Offset (Bytes)  Size    Type     Description
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
0-3             4       bytes    Magic Header ID (0x08200000)
4-7             4       uint32   Header Info
8-11            4       uint32   Payload Length (840 bytes)
12-15           4       uint32   Padding / Reserved
16-17           2       uint16   Spectrum Type (4=sample, 5=reference, 9=absorbance)
18-19           2       uint16   Channel Index (1=channel 1, 2=channel 2)
20-23           4       float32  Start Wavelength (190.0 nm)
24-27           4       float32  End Wavelength (390.0 nm)
28-31           4       float32  Wavelength Step (1.0 nm)
32-35           4       uint32   Number of Points (201 points)
36-839          804     float32  201 × 4-byte little-endian IEEE-754 floats
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Total: 840 bytes

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This guide explains how to operate the BioPAT® Spectro UV Server, configure the tecSaaS MPT UDP broadcast, and consume live 201-wavelength data in industrial SCADA and PAT platforms.

docs.title: The 201-Wavelength UV Spectrum
docs.text:
The spectrometer measures optical signals from 190.0 nm to 390.0 nm in 1.0 nm increments, yielding an array of exactly 201 float32 values:

wavelength_nm = 190.0 + index

spectrum[0]    # 190.0 nm
spectrum[90]   # 280.0 nm (UV protein absorption peak)
spectrum[200]  # 390.0 nm

docs.title: Data Types
docs.text:
For each acquisition cycle, the tec5 tecSaaS MPT software (driving the spectrometer) broadcasts 5 separate 840-byte UDP datagrams — one per data type below, each mapped to a specific tec5 type identifier:

Data Type Packet Type Redis Key OPC UA Tag Description Absorbance 9 absorbance_channel_1 absorbance_channel_1 Optical Absorbance ($A$) across 201 wavelengths Sample Intensity 4 sample_channel_1 sample_channel_1 Raw measurement intensity counts ($I$) Reference Intensity 5 onlinereference_channel_1 onlinereference_channel_1 Baseline reference intensity counts ($I_0$) Transmission 7 transmission_channel_1 transmission_channel_1 Transmittance ratio ($I / I_0$) Calibration 11 calibration_channel_1 calibration_channel_1 Dark / factory calibration baseline Wavelengths Axis (not stored in Redis — computed by opcserver) Wavelength Axis array [190.0, 191.0, ..., 390.0]

The _channel_1 suffix above comes from udpparser's UDP_CHANNEL_NAME setting, not from the packet itself — udpparser doesn't read the channel index in the UDP header, so this is a manual choice in compose.yaml/.env. If your instrument is wired to channel 2, set UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_2 and all the keys/tags above become ..._channel_2 instead. See Setup & Deployment.

docs.title: Connecting OPC UA Clients
docs.text: The OPC UA server listens on opc.tcp://<host>:4841 under namespace index 1 (http://biopat/spectrouv).

docs.title: Python Client Example (asyncua)
docs.text:
import asyncio
from asyncua import Client

async def read_spectrum():
    url = "opc.tcp://localhost:4841"
    async with Client(url=url) as client:
        # Access Channel 1 Absorbance variable node
        node = client.get_node("ns=1;s=absorbance_channel_1")
        absorbance_values = await node.read_value()

        # Access Wavelength axis
        wl_node = client.get_node("ns=1;s=Wavelength")
        wavelengths = await wl_node.read_value()

        print(f"Acquired {len(absorbance_values)} wavelength points:")
        print(f"  {wavelengths[90]} nm: {absorbance_values[90]:.4f} AU")

asyncio.run(read_spectrum())

docs.title: SCADA & Bioreactor Systems (Ignition, DeltaV, PCS 7)
docs.text:
1. Add an OPC UA connection to opc.tcp://<server_ip>:4841 (Security: None / Anonymous or configured).
  2. Browse to Objects -> spectrouv_1.
  3. Map absorbance_channel_1 as a 201-element float array tag.

docs.title: Testing with Mock Emitter
docs.text:
When testing without a physical spectrometer attached:

python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter --host 127.0.0.1 --port 20202

This broadcasts authentic 840-byte UDP packets containing simulated protein absorbance peaks at 280 nm.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: Get the BioPAT® Spectro UV Server running and publishing live 201-wavelength data in under 2 minutes!

docs.title: 1. Start the Docker Stack
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Sir-Narwhal/biopat-spectrouv-server.git
cd biopat-spectrouv-server

docker compose up -d

Verify that all four containers are healthy: 

docker compose ps

docs.title: 2. Test with Simulated Spectra (No Hardware Needed)
docs.text:
Launch the simulated UDP emitter:

python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter

You will see output showing periodic cycles of Reference, Sample Intensity, and Absorbance packets being transmitted to port 20202: 

[Mock Emitter] Broadcasting mock UDP spectral data to 127.0.0.1:20202...
[Mock Emitter] Cycle 1: Broadcasted sample, reference, and absorbance (201 wavelengths @ 190-390 nm)

docs.title: 3. Connect Your OPC UA Client
docs.text:
Connect to: 

opc.tcp://localhost:4841

In your OPC UA client (such as UaExpert): 1. Navigate to: Root -> Objects -> spectrouv_1. 2. Drag absorbance_channel_1, sample_channel_1, or Wavelength into the Data Access View. 3. Observe live array updates in real-time!

docs.title: Deployment Modes
docs.text: BioPAT® Spectro UV Server can be deployed in two modes: 1. Containerized (Recommended): Using Docker Compose. 2. Native: Running Python processes directly on the host.

docs.title: Configuration (.env)
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the project root:

cp .env.example .env

Default settings: 

UDP_IP=0.0.0.0
UDP_PORT=20202
UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_1

OPC_IP_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0
OPC_PORT_NUMBER=4841

REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=redisserver
REDIS_PORT_NUMBER=6379

docs.title: Channel Selection (Required)
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] UDP_CHANNEL_NAME is not read from the incoming UDP packets — udpparser never inspects the channel index in the packet header (bytes 18–19). It's decided entirely by this environment variable, so you must set it to match your actual spectrometer wiring:

  • Wired to channel 1: leave UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_1 (the default).
  • Wired to channel 2: set UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_2 in .env before starting the stack.
  • Both channels simultaneously: add a second udpparser service to compose.yaml (duplicate the existing one) with its own UDP_PORT and UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_2, and configure tecSaaS MPT to send that channel's UDP broadcast to the second port.

Getting this wrong doesn't error — it silently labels your data under the wrong channel's Redis keys and OPC UA nodes, so verify it explicitly rather than trusting the default.

docs.title: Launching Services
docs.text:
# Start in background
docker compose up -d

# View logs
docker compose logs -f udpparser
docker compose logs -f opcserver
docker compose logs -f udphelper

# Stop services
docker compose down

docs.title: Windows Tray App (Long-Running Deployments)
docs.text:
The MPT Guardian tray application is optional for short test sessions, but mandatory for any measurement session longer than ~6 hours — the tec5 tecSaaS MPT software intermittently stops transmitting UDP data on its own over extended runs, and MPT Guardian is what detects and restarts it. Install it via the installer, or run the included .exe directly with no build/install step.

MPT Guardian must run on the same Windows PC as the tec5 tecSaaS MPT software and this Docker Compose stack — it talks to redisserver over localhost and drives tecSaaS MPT via Windows UI Automation on the same desktop session, so it can't be split off onto a separate machine. In practice this means: when MPT Guardian is in use, deploy the whole stack via Docker Desktop on that same PC rather than on a separate Linux host.

docs.title: Offline / Air-Gapped Deployment
docs.text:
If the Windows PC can't reach Docker Hub (for example a locked-down lab PC), don't build on it — docker compose up --build has to download base images and Python packages, and fails with errors like lookup registry-1.docker.io: no such host. Instead, build once on a machine with internet access, export the images to .tar files, and load them on the offline PC.

On a machine with internet and Docker running:

export-docker-images.bat          rem or: export-docker-images.bat 1.0.1

This builds the udpparser, opcserver and udphelper images from app/Dockerfile, pulls redis:7-alpine, and saves each as a .tar in dist\docker-images\.

On the offline PC (copy the dist\docker-images folder and the repo, including compose.offline.yaml, across):

import-docker-images.bat           rem loads every .tar with "docker load"
run-docker-offline.bat             rem or: run-docker-offline.bat 1.0.1

run-docker-offline.bat starts the stack from compose.offline.yaml, which uses the loaded images (pull_policy: never) and never builds or pulls. The image tag must match the one used when exporting (latest if you didn't pass one). Use this instead of run-docker.bat on the offline PC.

compose.offline.yaml mirrors the service settings in compose.yaml — keep the two in sync when changing ports, environment variables, or services.

docs.title: Port Mappings
docs.text:
Ensure the following firewall ports are open on the server host:

Port Protocol Service Description 20202 UDP udpparser Receives UDP broadcast from tecSaaS MPT 4841 TCP opcserver OPC UA server endpoint for SCADA clients 6379 TCP redisserver Internal Redis state bus

The udphelper (watchdog) service exposes no ports — it only talks to redisserver over the internal Docker network.

docs.title: Issue: udpparser shows socket timeout or receives no packets
docs.text:
[UDP Parser] Socket timeout waiting for UDP broadcast; retrying...

Causes: 1. The spectrometer host PC is sending UDP packets to a different IP or port. 2. A firewall is blocking UDP port 20202.

Solutions: - In the recommended single-PC deployment, verify tecSaaS MPT is configured to send UDP packets to 127.0.0.1 (loopback) on port 20202, since udpparser runs on this same machine. If you're instead running the Docker stack on a separate host, verify it's targeting that host's IP on the same subnet. - Check if port 20202 is open and listening: 

# Windows
netstat -ano | findstr :20202
# Linux
ss -ulpn | grep 20202
- Send a test packet using the mock emitter: 
python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter --host 127.0.0.1 --port 20202

docs.title: Error: redis.exceptions.ConnectionError
docs.text:
redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error 111 connecting to localhost:6379

Solutions: 1. Verify the Redis container is running: 

docker compose ps redisserver
2. Test connection with redis-cli: 
docker compose exec redisserver redis-cli ping
# Expected: PONG
3. Inspect keys currently stored in Redis: 
docker compose exec redisserver redis-cli keys "*"

docs.title: Issue: Client connects but variables read [0.0, 0.0, ...]
docs.text:
Causes: - No UDP packets have been received in the last 5 seconds (keys expired in Redis). - udpparser is not running or connected to a different Redis instance.

Solutions: 1. Check udpparser logs: 

docker compose logs -f udpparser
2. Check if keys exist in Redis: 
docker compose exec redisserver redis-cli get absorbance_channel_1
3. Start the mock emitter to verify the pipeline: 
python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter

docs.title: 4. Port Conflicts
docs.text:
If port 4841 (OPC UA) or 20202 (UDP) is already in use by another application: 1. Open .env. 2. Change the host port mappings: 

UDP_PORT=20205
OPC_PORT_NUMBER=4845
3. Restart Docker Compose: 
docker compose up -d

docs.title: 5. Data Stops After Several Hours (Long-Running Sessions)
Issue: Spectral data was flowing fine, then silently went stale hours into a run
docs.text:
Cause: The tec5 tecSaaS MPT software intermittently stops transmitting UDP data on its own during long-running sessions (typically anywhere past ~6 hours). The udphelper watchdog will detect this (it sets mpt_refresh = "true" in Redis), but the Docker stack has no way to act on that signal by itself — something has to restart the tecSaaS MPT measurement session.

Solution: 1. Install and run the MPT Guardian tray application — either via the installer or by running the included .exe directly — on the same Windows PC that runs tecSaaS MPT and this Docker Compose stack (Guardian can't be split off onto a different machine; see tray_app/README.md). This is mandatory for any session longer than ~6 hours; short test/demo sessions can run without it. 2. Confirm it's running and polling by checking the mpt_refresh key: 

docker compose exec redisserver redis-cli get mpt_refresh
3. If MPT Guardian is already running and the feed is still stale, check its tray icon tooltip for Status: Error (Redis connection lost or state keys missing) and confirm redisserver's port 6379 is published to the host (docker compose ps) so Guardian's localhost:6379 connection can reach it.

docs.title: 6. Data Appears Under the Wrong Channel
Issue: Values show up under ..._channel_1 (or _channel_2) when you expected the other
docs.text:
Cause: udpparser does not read the channel index out of the UDP packet header — it tags every value it writes with whatever UDP_CHANNEL_NAME is set to in compose.yaml/.env (channel_1 by default), regardless of what the spectrometer actually sent. This is a manual setting, not an auto-detected one, and there's no error if it's wrong — the data just lands under the wrong keys.

Solutions: 1. Confirm which channel your instrument is actually wired to, then set it explicitly: 

# .env
UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_2
2. Restart the stack so udpparser picks up the change: 
docker compose up -d
3. To ingest both channels at the same time, you need two udpparser instances — duplicate the service in compose.yaml with a different UDP_PORT and UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_2, and point tecSaaS MPT's second channel broadcast at that port. 4. Verify the fix by checking which key actually has fresh data: 
docker compose exec redisserver redis-cli get absorbance_channel_2

docs.title: 7. Build Fails With no such host / Can't Reach Docker Hub
Error: failed to resolve source metadata for docker.io/... / lookup registry-1.docker.io: no such host
docs.text:
Cause: docker compose up --build (and run-docker.bat) need internet access to pull the base images and install Python packages. A PC with no internet or blocked DNS can't build.

Solution: build on a machine that has internet, export the images, and run them on the offline PC without building — see Offline / Air-Gapped Deployment. If the PC should have internet, check DNS (nslookup registry-1.docker.io) and any proxy settings in Docker Desktop instead.

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter
docs.text: Testing utility for broadcasting synthetic 840-byte tec5 UDP datagrams without physical spectrometer hardware.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter --host 127.0.0.1 --port 20202 --interval 1.0

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --host: Target host (default: 127.0.0.1)
  • --port: Target UDP port (default: 20202)
  • --interval: Broadcast cycle interval in seconds (default: 1.0)
  • --channel: Channel index (default: 1)

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.opcua_server
docs.text: This module implements an OPC UA server that publishes UV-Vis spectral data for real-time access by industrial control systems and SCADA platforms.

docs.title: Function: opcua_loop()
docs.text: async def opcua_loop(redis_client: redis.Redis) -> None:

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Run the OPC UA server and continuously publish spectral data from Redis to connected SCADA clients.

Creates an OPC UA server registered under the http://biopat/spectrouv namespace, containing two spectrometer channels (spectrouv_1, spectrouv_2). Each channel exposes five spectral data types (transmission, absorbance, onlinereference, sample, calibration) plus a read-only wavelength axis and intensity/reference_intensity aliases. The server polls Redis every 1 second for updated spectral values and pushes them to OPC UA clients, enabling real-time subscription and monitoring.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: redis_client: redis.Redis - An active Redis connection (authenticated and validated) - Port: 6379 (default) or as configured - Must have decode_responses=True for string operations - Example: redis.Redis(host="localhost", port=6379, decode_responses=True)

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: None - Function runs indefinitely until process termination - Blocks the calling coroutine

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The function executes an infinite async loop with these steps:

  1. Initialization (runs once)
  2. Creates OPC UA Server instance
  3. Registers the http://biopat/spectrouv namespace
  4. Creates two channel objects (spectrouv_1, spectrouv_2)
  5. For each channel and datatype, creates writable OPC UA variables

  6. Creates read-only wavelength axis variable (190-390 nm, 201 points)

  7. Polling Loop (repeats every 1 second)

  8. Scans Redis for keys matching patterns: transmission*, absorbance*, etc.
  9. For each key found:
    • Retrieves JSON-encoded spectral data from Redis
    • Identifies target channel (channel_1 or channel_2)
    • Updates corresponding OPC UA variable with new values
  10. Sleeps 1 second before next poll
  11. Catches and logs exceptions (continues operating if errors occur)

docs.title: OPC UA Namespace Structure
docs.text:
ns=1 (http://biopat/spectrouv)
├── spectrouv_1 (Object)
│   ├── transmission_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── absorbance_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── onlinereference_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── sample_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── calibration_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   └── Wavelength (Variable, 201 floats, read-only)
└── spectrouv_2 (Object)
    ├── transmission_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── absorbance_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── onlinereference_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── sample_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── calibration_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    └── Wavelength (Variable, 201 floats, read-only)

docs.title: Data Type Definitions
docs.text:
Each datatype variable contains 201 floating-point values:

Datatype Meaning Source transmission Raw transmission spectrum (I/I₀) Direct measurement absorbance Calculated absorbance (A = -log₁₀T) Derived from transmission onlinereference Reference/calibration spectrum Stored calibration sample Active sample measurement Current measurement calibration Calibration data used Reference baseline

docs.title: Wavelength Axis
docs.text:
• 201 values from 190.0 to 390.0 nm (inclusive)
  • Spacing: 1.0 nm between consecutive values
  • Read-only: Cannot be modified via OPC UA clients

docs.title: Redis Key Naming Convention
docs.text:
The server scans Redis for keys following this pattern:

{datatype}_{channel}

Examples:
transmission_channel_1
absorbance_channel_2
onlinereference_channel_1

Valid pattern components:

Component Valid Values {datatype} transmission, absorbance, onlinereference, sample, calibration {channel} channel_1, channel_2

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configuration is via environment variables:

REDIS_IP_ADDRESS = os.environ.get("REDIS_IP_ADDRESS", "localhost")
REDIS_PORT_NUMBER = int(os.environ.get("REDIS_PORT_NUMBER", 6379))
OPC_IP_ADDRESS = os.environ.get("OPC_IP_ADDRESS", "0.0.0.0")
OPC_PORT_NUMBER = int(os.environ.get("OPC_PORT_NUMBER", 4841))
Variable Default Purpose REDIS_IP_ADDRESS localhost (redisserver inside Docker Compose) Redis host IP REDIS_PORT_NUMBER 6379 Redis port OPC_IP_ADDRESS 0.0.0.0 OPC UA listen address (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces) OPC_PORT_NUMBER 4841 OPC UA port (standard)

docs.title: Exceptions & Error Handling
docs.text:
The function catches and logs exceptions internally, allowing the server to continue operating even if errors occur:

Common exceptions:

Exception Cause Recovery redis.ConnectionError Redis unavailable Retries next poll json.JSONDecodeError Invalid JSON in Redis Logs warning, skips key KeyError Channel not recognized Logs warning, skips value Exception General error Logged, server continues

All exceptions are logged via Python logging at WARNING level.

docs.title: Basic Startup
docs.text:
import redis
import asyncio
from parselibrary.opcua_server import opcua_loop

async def main():
    # Connect to Redis
    r = redis.Redis(host='localhost', port=6379, decode_responses=True)

    # Run OPC UA server
    await opcua_loop(r)

# Run forever
asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Command-line Execution
docs.text:
# With environment variables
export REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=192.168.1.10
export OPC_PORT_NUMBER=8841
python -m parselibrary.opcua_server

docs.title: Docker Container
docs.text:
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY parselibrary/ parselibrary/
ENV REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=redis
ENV OPC_IP_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0
CMD ["python", "-m", "parselibrary.opcua_server"]

docs.title: Publishing Data to Redis
docs.text:
opcua_loop only reads from Redis — it never touches the network. Any process that writes a 201-element JSON float array to a {datatype}_{channel} key (see udp_parser.main_loop) will have it picked up on the next 1-second poll:

import json
import redis

r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

# Publish 201 synthetic values for OPC UA server to pick up
spectrum = [0.0] * 201
r.set("transmission_channel_1", json.dumps(spectrum), ex=5)

# Server will pick this up in next polling cycle (~1 second)
print("Spectrum published")

docs.title: Connecting OPC UA Client
docs.text:
import asyncio
from asyncua import Client

async def connect():
    client = Client("opc.tcp://localhost:4841")
    async with client:
        # Browse namespace
        root = client.get_root_node()
        objects = await root.get_children()

        # Get transmission data for channel 1
        node = client.get_node("ns=1;s=transmission_channel_1")
        value = await node.read_value()

        print(f"Got {len(value)} wavelength points")
        print(f"First 5 values: {value[:5]}")

        # Subscribe to changes
        async def on_change(node, var):
            print(f"Value changed: {var}")

        handler = await node.subscribe_value(on_change)

        # Keep connection open
        await asyncio.sleep(10)

asyncio.run(connect())

docs.title: Performance Characteristics
docs.text:
• Polling latency: ~1 second (the asyncio.sleep(1.0) at the end of the polling loop)
  • OPC UA update frequency: 1 Hz
  • Redis scan time: ~5-50 ms per poll (depends on key count)
  • Memory overhead: ~5 MB for 2 channels × 5 datatypes × 201 values
  • Max concurrent clients: 10-50 (asyncio limited)

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Events are logged at level INFO by default (configured in source):

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

Change level for more verbose output:

import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

docs.title: Related Functions

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.udp_parser
docs.text: The UDP Parser service receives, validates, and decodes incoming 840-byte UDP spectral broadcast datagrams from the tec5 tecSaaS MPT software (the vendor control application, not the spectrometer hardware itself — see Architecture). Each acquisition cycle sends up to 5 separate 840-byte datagrams, one per data type (sample, onlinereference, transmission, absorbance, calibration).

docs.title: unpack_udp(binary_string: bytes) -> List[float]
docs.text: Extracts the 201 float32 values from an incoming 840-byte datagram payload.

docs.title: collect_mpt_spectra(udp: socket.socket) -> Dict[str, List[float]]
docs.text:
Reads a batch of datagrams from the UDP socket and maps tec5 packet type integers to spectral identifiers: - Type 4 → sample (Sample Intensity) - Type 5 → onlinereference (Reference Intensity) - Type 7 → transmission - Type 9 → absorbance - Type 11 → calibration

Skips control datagrams (144 or 72 bytes) and any packet that isn't exactly 840 bytes or doesn't carry a recognized type.

docs.title: main_loop(r: Redis, udp: socket.socket) -> None
docs.text: Runs one ingestion cycle: calls collect_mpt_spectra, then writes each spectral array to Redis as {type}_{UDP_CHANNEL_NAME} with a 5-second TTL (ex=5). sample is also mirrored to intensity_{channel} and onlinereference to reference_intensity_{channel} for more intuitive SCADA tag names.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configured via environment variables (see Setup & Deployment):

Variable Default Purpose UDP_IP 0.0.0.0 Listen address for spectrometer UDP datagrams UDP_PORT 20202 Port receiving tec5 UDP broadcasts UDP_CHANNEL_NAME channel_1 Redis key suffix identifying this channel REDIS_IP_ADDRESS localhost Redis host (redisserver inside Docker Compose) REDIS_PORT_NUMBER 6379 Redis port

[!IMPORTANT] UDP_CHANNEL_NAME is not auto-detected — you must set it manually. Every tec5 UDP packet does carry a channel index in its header (byte offset 18–19, see Architecture), but collect_mpt_spectra/unpack_udp never read it. The channel a given udpparser instance writes to is decided entirely by this environment variable. If your spectrometer is wired to channel 2 and you leave UDP_CHANNEL_NAME at its channel_1 default, the data will silently land under ..._channel_1 keys — verify this setting in compose.yaml/.env for your actual hardware before trusting any channel-tagged data. To ingest both channels simultaneously, run a second udpparser instance (a duplicated Compose service) with UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_2 and a distinct UDP_PORT.

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.spectrouv_helper
docs.text: This module implements a lightweight Redis watchdog that detects when live spectral data has gone stale and signals the optional Windows tray companion to restart the spectrometer's measurement session. It runs as the udphelper container in the Docker Compose stack.

docs.title: Function: watchdog_cycle()
docs.text: async def watchdog_cycle(r_spectrouv: Redis, set_mptrefresh: bool) -> bool:

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Runs a single watchdog check and returns the updated set_mptrefresh flag for the caller to pass into the next cycle.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
r_spectrouv: Redis - An active Redis connection - Must have decode_responses=True for string operations

set_mptrefresh: bool - Tracks whether a refresh has already been requested for the current stale period, so the flag is only raised once per outage - Pass False on the first call

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: bool - The updated set_mptrefresh state to pass into the next call

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Reads the absorbance_channel_1 key from Redis.
  2. If the key is missing (expired TTL — no fresh UDP data in the last 5 seconds) and a refresh hasn't already been requested, sets mpt_refresh = "true" in Redis, logs a warning, and marks set_mptrefresh = True.
  3. If the key is present, logs the point count at DEBUG level and resets set_mptrefresh = False, re-arming the watchdog so it can raise the flag again if data goes stale a second time.
  4. Sleeps 1 second before returning.

Note that watchdog_cycle only ever sets mpt_refresh to "true" — it never clears it back to "false". The tray application is responsible for clearing the key once it has handled the refresh.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configured via environment variables (see Setup & Deployment):

Variable Default Purpose REDIS_IP_ADDRESS localhost Redis host (redisserver inside Docker Compose) REDIS_PORT_NUMBER 6379 Redis port

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import asyncio
from redis import Redis
from parselibrary.spectrouv_helper import watchdog_cycle

async def main():
    r = Redis(host="localhost", port=6379, decode_responses=True)
    set_mptrefresh = False
    while True:
        set_mptrefresh = await watchdog_cycle(r, set_mptrefresh)

asyncio.run(main())
